headline: US stocks fell as Treasury yields rebounded and Walmart results pressured defensives despite supportive Treasury buyback signals
raw_text:
- Dow (DIA), S&P 500 (SPY), and Nasdaq (QQQ) all closed lower, reversing the prior session’s gains and putting major indexes on pace for weekly losses
- Treasury yields rebounded, with the 10-year climbing above 4.7% and the 30-year near 5.24%, weighing on equities and rate-sensitive groups
- Consumer staples and other defensive sectors lagged after Walmart (WMT) dropped sharply on its slowest U.S. comparable sales growth in years at 2.6% versus expectations near 3.7%
- Walmart (WMT)’s U.S. comps miss and lower Q3 EPS guidance overshadowed other results
- Moderna (MRNA) fell more than 20% on profit-taking after Wednesday’s large gain on positive cancer vaccine data
- Crypto-related names outperformed as MARA Holdings (MARA) jumped alongside Bitcoin (@BTC) strength and sentiment improved on President Trump’s support and developments around the CLARITY Act
- Energy edged higher as oil (@CL) prices moved amid Trump’s economic pressure campaign toward Iran
- Most other sectors, including consumer discretionary, parts of tech, and small caps, declined in response to the bond-market reversal
- After-hours trading was muted, with Walmart (WMT) edging higher and Moderna (MRNA) seeing limited further downside, and traders looking ahead to additional earnings, bond-market moves, Treasury buyback details, Fed commentary, and upcoming economic data
